The result is then passed to handleLarkError (not shown, so its exact validation is unverifiable), which presumably expects Lark's envelope. Unlike Google/Zoom/O365, Lark's path doesn't use parseRefreshTokenResponse to normalize. Mechanism is grounded in the diff; exact failure depends on unseen handleLarkError.

judged_text: In sharing mode the value passed to handleLarkError is the sync contract {access_token, expiry}, which lacks Lark's required code/msg/data envelope, so the Lark-shape validation rejects it (or yields undefined nested data). Under credential sync every Lark token refresh throws, so Lark calendar operations fail for self-hosters using the sync endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call is wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and the returned `resp` is always passed into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` explicitly changes behavior under sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) to call the external sync endpoint, whose inline comment says its response "should only contain the access token and expiry date"—i.e., not necessarily Lark’s native refresh response shape. This creates a shape/contract mismatch: `handleLarkError` is designed for Lark API responses, so under credential sync it may reject/throw when given a non-Lark response, breaking Lark token refresh and thus Lark calendar operations for sync users.
